title: Broken: My Story of Addiction and Redemption
author: William Cope Moyers with Katherine Ketcham
target_audience: Individuals and families affected by addiction
People interested in personal stories of recovery
Readers seeking understanding of substance abuse
General audiences interested in memoirs about personal struggle and transformation
core_themes: Addiction and its personal, familial, and societal impacts
The journey to recovery and the process of redemption
Resilience and hope in the face of repeated relapse
The importance of support systems (family, treatment, spiritual communities)
primary_purpose: To provide a candid and raw personal account of substance addiction, its devastating effects, and the ongoing process of recovery—offering hope and insight for those struggling with addiction and for their loved ones.

structure_format.narrative_style: First-person, honest, and emotionally detailed memoir
structure_format.organization: Chronological account, interspersed with reflection and insight
features: Exploration of family and professional life
Examination of the recovery process and relapse
Discussions about stigma, treatment methods, and advocacy

key_concepts_lessons: Addiction can affect anyone, regardless of background or upbringing.
Denial and secrecy fuel the cycle of addiction.
Relapse does not mean failure; recovery is an ongoing and non-linear process.
Support—both personal and professional—is essential to overcoming addiction.
Open dialogue about substance abuse helps break down stigma.
Personal honesty and accountability are critical to long-term recovery.
notable_features: Written by the son of journalist Bill Moyers, adding public resonance
Honest portrayal of repeated relapse and the complexity of recovery
Combines personal experience with broader discussion of addiction in America
Blends memoir with advocacy for better treatment and understanding
cultural_historical_context: Published in the mid-2000s, when addiction was becoming more widely discussed in the media, 'Broken' brought attention to the realities of substance abuse in families perceived as successful or privileged, challenging stereotypes and encouraging national conversation.
reception_impact: Praised for its honesty and courage in addressing personal and family issues
Used as a resource in support groups and addiction counseling settings
Helped reduce stigma by showing addiction's wide reach
Appreciated for its practical insights into the journey of recovery
comparable_titles: Tweak: Growing Up on Methamphetamines by Nic Sheff
Lit: A Memoir by Mary Karr
Portrait of an Addict as a Young Man by Bill Clegg
